lesson: The office units are rooms 301, 401 and 501 on L3, L4 and L5 (about 208-225 m2 each, empty apart from ceiling lights). L2 has live/work units, studios and the Mezzanine Dining room, not offices.

Office Unit 301 (L3, 225 m2) fits 24 workstations in 4-desk pods at 1.2 m aisles (22 at 10 m2 per person). The Mezzanine Dining room (200, L2, 79 m2) only takes 5-6 round 60-inch tables with safe aisles.
Furniture on the mezzanine is hosted on level M1, not L2. Room levels and furniture levels can differ: check the level of existing furniture before placing more.

Chair-Breuer (and chairs nested in 'Table-Dining Round w Chairs') face local +Y when unrotated, with the origin at the seat centre. To seat someone at a desk, place the chair about 100 mm beyond the desk edge, rotated to face the desk.
Table-Rectangular's insertion point is the table centre; its type parameters Length (along local X) and Width (local Y) give the footprint. It works as a desk (e.g. 66" x 30").

For layouts in a room, sample the room once on a 100 mm grid with Room.IsPointInRoom and then test candidates against that grid: this is 5-10 times faster than calling IsPointInRoom for every test point. The test_fit_out script shows the pattern.

When collecting obstacles in a room with BoundingBoxIntersectsFilter, cameras (3D views), spaces, area boundary and sketch lines match too and block everything. Keep only physical FamilyInstances (not panels or mullions), railings and stairs, and skip boxes larger than about 10 m.
A view whose crop is controlled by a scope box ignores CropBox changes. For a picture of an area, create a temporary ViewPlan or isometric View3D (inside a dry run it disappears with the rollback).
doc.ExportImage works inside an open transaction group, so a dry run can take pictures of the proposed change before it is rolled back (preview_image: true does this automatically).
Do not assume where room types are from the level you are looking at: read get_model_brief first. In one test Claude looked for offices on L2 only and concluded the building had none.

When showing options (A, B, C) in a demo, open the plan with open_view first and preview each option with its own transaction_name: every preview keeps its own Apply card. Call pending_changes before telling the user which cards exist; in one demo Claude wrongly said only the last option remained.
RequestViewChange does not reliably switch views when Revit is not the focused window; open_view sets UIDocument.ActiveView directly and zooms to the room.
